name: Borexino — axion searches
summary: A liquid-scintillator solar-neutrino detector that also searches for solar axions and ALPs; this record focuses on its dark-matter-candidate studies.
detection_principle: Solar p+d reactions produce 5.5 MeV axions that can deposit visible energy through inverse Primakoff conversion, Compton-like conversion, the axioelectric effect or two-photon decay.

sites.name: INFN Laboratori Nazionali del Gran Sasso，Assergi
sites.location: INFN Laboratori Nazionali del Gran Sasso，Assergi

status.label: The documented historical experimental phase is complete
status.evidence: The collaboration's 2025 paper explicitly uses the full Borexino dataset. This status denotes completed detector data-taking; analysis may continue.

results.summary: The full 2025 dataset showed no signal. For mA<1 MeV it sets coupling-product bounds |gAγ g3AN|≤2.3×10⁻¹¹ GeV⁻¹ and |gAe g3AN|≤1.9×10⁻¹³ (90% CL).

science_scope: Primarily searches for solar-produced axions or hidden photons as complementary tests of dark-matter candidates. Solar flux is distinct from cold Galactic-halo dark matter; a solar-axion discovery alone would not establish the composition of cosmic dark matter.
